name: Usine Claude et Duval
key_features: Le Corbusier's only factory: reinforced concrete on stilts, with a roof terrace and a hung sunshade screen.

name: Notre-Dame-de-Toute-Grâce du Plateau d'Assy
key_features: Alpine church facing Mont Blanc, decorated by Léger, Chagall, Bonnard, Matisse and others.

name: Garabit Viaduct
key_features: Wrought-iron parabolic arch, 165 m main span, 124 m above the Truyère river.

name: Le CentQuatre
by: Édouard Delebarre de Bay and Godon (1874); Atelier Novembre (2008)
key_features: Former municipal undertaker's hall in cast iron, glass and brick, reopened as an arts centre in 2008.

name: Hôtel de Ville de Boulogne-Billancourt
key_features: Reinforced-concrete Art Deco town hall with a 19-bay symmetrical front and a 65 m guichets hall.

name: Villa Arson
key_features: Hillside art school and centre of about 23,000 m2 built around courtyards, terraces and gardens facing the Riviera.

name: Roma Termini
key_features: Long glazed hall under a concrete roof shaped as a flattened arch, with a cantilevered entrance canopy.

name: Stadio dei Marmi
key_features: Plain white marble stadium ringed by sixty 4 m Carrara marble athlete statues by 24 sculptors.

name: Villa Necchi Campiglio
key_features: Rationalist villa in a walled garden, with Milan's first private heated swimming pool and a glazed winter garden.

name: Torre Galfa
key_features: 109 m tower on a rectangular plan; concrete frame almost hidden behind a glass and aluminium curtain wall.

name: Lingotto
key_features: Five-storey Fiat factory where cars rose through the building to a rooftop test track reached by spiral ramps.

name: Santa Maria Consolatrice al Tiburtino
key_features: Minimalist parish church begun in 1942 and consecrated in 1945, on Piazza Santa Maria Consolatrice.

name: Palazzo della Farnesina
by: Enrico Del Debbio, Arnaldo Foschini, Vittorio Ballio Morpurgo
key_features: Nine-storey travertine-faced ministry with over 1,300 rooms, about 169 m wide; designed 1935, finished 1959.

name: Palazzo del Cinema, Venice Lido
key_features: Rationalist festival palace of 1937 with a 1,000-seat Sala Grande; partly extended in 1952 with a forepart and arena.

name: Fondazione Querini Stampalia (Scarpa ground floor and garden)
key_features: Scarpa's ground floor, entrance bridge, courtyard garden with Deluigi mosaic and fountain, in a historic palazzo.

name: Stadio Olimpico
by: Luigi Moretti, Carlo Valle, Annibale Vitellozzi
key_features: 1990 roof: a Teflon-coated fibreglass membrane hung from 88 radial cables between steel rings on 12 pillars.

name: Ponte della Costituzione
key_features: Arched truss bridge over the Grand Canal: 180 m radius, 79.72 m longest span, 7.04 m clearance at high tide.

name: Roma Tiburtina station
key_features: Glazed bridge-station 240 m long and 50 m wide, suspended 9 m above ground, with 29 escalators and 52 lifts.

name: Intesa Sanpaolo Skyscraper
key_features: 167 m bioclimatic tower, naturally ventilated, with south-facade photovoltaics and a rooftop greenhouse restaurant.

name: Napoli Afragola station
key_features: Four-level, 25 m bridge building over four tracks, with a 20,000 m2 concourse.

name: Museion
key_features: Prism 54 m long, 25 m high, 23 m wide, with transparent front and rear facades linking two parts of the city.

name: Kensal House
key_features: Two curved blocks of 68 housing association flats.

name: King's Cross station
key_features: Two great arched train sheds and a clock tower; 2012 concourse has a semi-circular roof.

name: Pallant House Gallery
by: Colin St John Wilson and MJ Long (2006 extension)
key_features: Believed the first UK art gallery heated and cooled by a geothermal system.

name: The Whitworth
key_features: Gallery wings are joined by a glass promenade.

name: Embassy of Denmark, London
key_features: Called a stark architectural grid of grey modernism, with a geometric concrete mural by Ole Schwalbe.

name: Palm House, Kew Gardens
key_features: Described as the first large-scale structural use of wrought iron, with an upper walkway.

name: Royal Pavilion
key_features: Bulbous domes and chhatri-topped minarets.

name: Spire of Dublin
key_features: Eight hollow stainless steel cone sections, with two tuned mass dampers inside.

name: Golden Lane Estate
key_features: 1950s council housing complex with maisonette blocks faced in primary-colour panels and a 16-storey tower.

name: Southwark tube station
key_features: Jubilee line station whose upper concourse is the centrepiece, with a 40 m glass wall of 660 blue glass pieces.

name: St Pancras railway station
key_features: Wrought-iron pillars carry a single-span roof that was the largest in the world when completed.

name: Livingstone Tower
key_features: Curtain wall of opaque dark green glass spandrel panels framed by orange metal uprights.

name: Scottish Storytelling Centre
key_features: Purpose-built storytelling centre that incorporates John Knox House.

name: Swansea Civic Centre
by: C. W. Quick (West Glamorgan County Architects Department)
key_features: Brutalist county building with continuous bands of glazing between deep calcined-flint panels.

name: Peace Bridge (Foyle)
key_features: Asymmetrical self-anchored suspension bridge for cyclists and pedestrians, supported by two sloping pillars.

name: Gorilla House, London Zoo
key_features: White cylindrical drum in 10 cm reinforced concrete, with a rotating semi-circular top-hung screen.

name: Tate St Ives
key_features: Gallery above Porthmeor Beach with a central rotunda, styled after the site's former gasworks.

name: Glasgow Tower
key_features: Aerofoil-shaped observation tower able to rotate 360 degrees into the wind.

name: St Albert's Catholic Chaplaincy
key_features: New chapel behind the 1779 house, with an altar window giving a clear view of the garden; RIBA-honoured.

name: Heathrow Terminal 5
key_features: Four storeys under a single-span undulating steel roof, with glass facades.

name: Sun House
key_features: Modernist house on Frognal Way, Hampstead; Grade II* listed.

name: Saïd Business School
key_features: Built on the former Rewley Road station site opposite Oxford railway station.

name: Weston Library
key_features: Scott's New Bodleian: deep stacks behind elevations no higher than their neighbours; 11-storey bookstack.

name: Manchester Civil Justice Centre
key_features: Cantilevered 'fingers' at each end and a suspended glass wall, the largest in Europe.

name: Royal Liver Building
key_features: Crowned by a pair of clock towers; an early reinforced-concrete building.

name: Red House
key_features: L-shaped plan with a high-pitched red tile roof; windows placed to suit the rooms, not symmetry.

name: Dynamic Earth
key_features: Steel mast-supported membrane over a steel skeleton; keeps the old Abbey Brewery wall.

name: Queen's Cross Church
key_features: Timber-lined barrel-vaulted nave roof; pulpit carved in Mackintosh designs.

name: Pierhead Building
key_features: Highly ornamental clock tower; exterior finished in glazed terracotta blocks.

name: Ulster Museum
key_features: Brutalist extension with great cubic projections and cantilevers.

name: Knock Basilica
by: Daithi Hanly (with Louis J Brennan, Brian Brennan)
key_features: Designed in a modern style in concrete.

name: Lys Kernow (New County Hall)
by: Francis Kenneth Hicklin and Alan Groves
key_features: A three-storey square concrete-framed Brutalist block with a council chamber cantilevered out on the east side.

name: Eltham Palace (Courtauld house)
key_features: 1930s house joined to a medieval great hall, with Art Deco interiors called a masterpiece of modern design.

name: Hornsey Town Hall
key_features: Called the first major UK building built in the Modernist style, with a tall tower at the courtyard corner.

name: Shell Centre
by: Howard Robertson and Ralph Maynard Smith
key_features: A 27-storey, 107 m tower clad in Portland stone, which has weathered better than many contemporaries.

name: Newcastle Civic Centre
key_features: Modern sculptures by David Wynne and abstract murals by Victor Pasmore are part of the building.

name: Palace of Westminster
key_features: Perpendicular Gothic Revival style with ornate decoration, designed by a classical architect.

name: Royal Crescent
key_features: A crescent of 30 houses with 114 Ionic columns on the first floor under a Palladian entablature.

name: London Stadium
key_features: A lightweight demountable steel and precast concrete upper tier, with a cable-supported roof.

name: Waterfront Hall
key_features: A copper-coated dome and a flexible auditorium whose stalls seating can be moved to form a larger arena.

name: Glasgow Science Centre
by: Building Design Partnership (Glasgow Tower: Richard Horden)
key_features: Science Mall evokes the canted hull of a ship; the Glasgow Tower is a freely-rotating tower.

name: Tower Bridge
key_features: Combines bascule, suspension and (until 1960) cantilever types, with central bascules that open for ships.

name: Wolfson College, Oxford
key_features: Three quadrangles, including a Tree Quad built around existing trees and a River Quad with a punt harbour.

name: First Unitarian Church of Rochester
key_features: Deeply folded brick walls with thin two-storey light hoods that shield the windows from direct sun.

name: Kleinhans Music Hall
key_features: Concert hall by father and son with two performance spaces; a National Historic Landmark for its architecture.

name: Harbor Towers
by: Henry N. Cobb (I. M. Pei & Partners)
key_features: Two 40-storey residential towers on the Boston waterfront, part of the 1960s harbour revitalisation.

name: Murray D. Lincoln Campus Center
key_features: A concrete high-rise with an attached parking garage; its hotel occupies floors three to seven.

name: Power Center for the Performing Arts
by: Kevin Roche John Dinkeloo and Associates
key_features: Proscenium-stage theatre on the University of Michigan's central campus, opened 1971.

name: Richards Medical Research Laboratories
key_features: Laboratory towers around a central service tower, with brick shafts for stairs and ducts and exposed precast structure.

name: Douglas and Charlotte Grant House
key_features: Usonian house on 40 acres with window walls, horizontal bands of windows and natural materials.

name: Home Building Association Bank
key_features: One of eight banks by Sullivan; a narrow lot made larger by building two storeys.

name: Hubert H. Humphrey Building
key_features: Eight-storey Brutalist headquarters of Health and Human Services; one of Breuer's two federal buildings in Washington.

name: Kips Bay Towers
by: I. M. Pei & S. J. Kessler
key_features: Two 20-storey Brutalist towers with 1,118 units across three blocks, built as middle-income rental housing.

name: Munson-Williams-Proctor Arts Institute
key_features: Regional art museum and performing-arts centre in Utica, designed by Philip Johnson.

name: North Shore Congregation Israel
key_features: Reform synagogue on Sheridan Road designed by Minoru Yamasaki.

name: Oakes Ames Memorial Hall
key_features: Richardson hall with landscaping by Frederick Law Olmsted, beside the Ames Free Library.

name: Olivetti-Underwood Factory
key_features: Typewriter factory commissioned from Kahn in 1966 by Olivetti, patrons of industrial design.

name: Reynolds Metals Company International Headquarters
key_features: Low-rise office in a landscape by Charles F. Gillette; cited as a prototype of suburban office development.

name: Richard H. Mandel House
key_features: Z-shaped International Style house with flat roof, smooth walls, projecting balconies and wide expanses of glass.

name: River City
key_features: Mixed-use building that shares elements with Goldberg's Marina City.

name: Rockefeller Guest House
key_features: Johnson's only private residence in New York City; a dark red brick ground floor under a glass storey.

name: Sciences Library (SciLi)
key_features: A 180-foot Brutalist high-rise library at Brown University.

name: Seventeenth Church of Christ, Scientist
key_features: Circular concrete church with no traditional windows in the amphitheatre; light comes through a skylight.

name: Thomas Crane Public Library
key_features: Richardsonian Romanesque library funded by the Crane family as a memorial.

name: Unitarian Universalist Church of Arlington
key_features: Concrete Brutalist sanctuary designed by local architect Charles M. Goodman in 1964.

name: United States Tax Court Building
key_features: Courthouse and landscaped plaza occupying a whole block in Judiciary Square.

name: Van Allen Building
key_features: Four-storey department store, a National Historic Landmark since 1976 for its architecture.

name: W. E. B. Du Bois Library
key_features: At 28 storeys, the third-tallest library in the world.

name: W. R. Grace Building
key_features: Skyscraper overlooking Bryant Park and the New York Public Library's main branch.

name: Watergate Complex
key_features: Six buildings of apartments, a hotel and offices on ten acres, built 1963–71.

name: Evans Hall
key_features: Statistics, economics and maths building known for many windowless classrooms.

name: Hallidie Building
key_features: One of the country's first glass curtain walls.

name: Horatio West Court
key_features: Six small attached flat-roofed cubes around a driveway; Mission Revival arched entries.

name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco
key_features: Atrium lobby 107 m long, 49 m wide, 52 m high, a record for a hotel lobby.

name: Los Angeles County Hall of Records
key_features: Aluminum louvers run the height of the south face, once designed to turn with the sun.

name: Mark Taper Forum
key_features: Perfectly circular, exterior drum wrapped in precast relief by Jacques Overhoff.

name: Pacific Design Center
key_features: Center Blue, the 'Blue Whale', is clad in bright blue glass.

name: Parker Center
key_features: Eight-story reinforced concrete; west elevation covered in ceramic tile.

name: Pearlman Mountain Cabin
key_features: Cylindrical cabin on a boulder, flat roof held by encircling tree trunks.
